title: What keeps pulling you in
text: Six questions about real situations. Not “what is your why” — but what you worked on, what annoys you and what you changed. What repeats in those stories is the direction.

guidance.title: Before you start
guidance.time: Take your time. Twenty to thirty minutes, and it gets better if you are not doing something else alongside.
guidance.save: It saves automatically while you write — even if something crashes. You can pause any time and continue later.
guidance.stories: Tell one thing that happened, rather than describing yourself. One example is worth more than a summary.
guidance.private: Everything you write here is visible only to you. It feeds no search, no matching and no profile unless you release it explicitly.
guidance.noTest: This is not a test. There are no points, no type and no category — at the end you see what repeats in your examples, and you decide what fits.

notice.paused: Saved. You can continue any time.
notice.completed: The conversation is complete. Your answers are below.

errors.start: The conversation could not be opened. Please try again.
errors.short: A little more — at least ten characters.
errors.long: That is longer than two thousand characters. Please shorten it.
errors.save: The answer could not be saved. The text is still there, please try again.
errors.complete: Completing did not work. Please try again.
errors.stale: This question is no longer the current one. Below is where you stand.
errors.too_few: A summary needs at least four answers.
errors.statement_long: That is longer than two hundred characters. Shorten it to one sentence.

progress.answered: {count, plural, =0 {none answered yet} =1 {1 answered} other {# answered}}
progress.enough: That is enough for a summary. More makes it more precise.

review.title: Your answers
review.text: Read side by side, what repeats often shows itself.
review.pendingSummary: The summary — which themes and changes keep coming back for you — is not generated automatically yet. Until then your answers are the result.

interview.answerHint: At least {min} characters. Take your space — one situation, not a conclusion.
interview.tooShort: Still too short — at least {min} characters.
interview.restored: There was still a text in this browser, longer than the saved one. It is here now.
interview.saveStateFailed: Not saved — the text is still in this browser
interview.followUpHint: These follow-ups belong to the same answer — just keep writing.

more_of_this.title: Tell me about something you worked on where you thought: I would like to do more of that.
more_of_this.hint: Professional or personal — both count equally.

followUps.whatMattered: What exactly about it mattered to you?
followUps.doingOrResult: Was it more about what you did — or about what came out of it?

keeps_bothering.title: Which problem or situation keeps annoying you because you think: surely this could be better?
keeps_bothering.hint: Not today's annoyance, but the one that keeps returning.

followUps.whatExactlyBothers: What exactly about it bothers you again and again?
followUps.whoIsAffected: Who do you think this problem is particularly relevant for?

changed_something.title: When did you last feel that your work or your actions really changed something meaningful?
changed_something.hint: Something small counts too. What matters is that it actually happened.

followUps.whatWasDifferentAfter: What was actually different for somebody afterwards?
followUps.whyThisMattered: Why was this particular change important?

change_in_others.title: Which change in other people or in your surroundings makes you especially glad when you were part of it?
change_in_others.hint: This is about the effect, not about your activity.

followUps.howYouNoticed: How did you notice that something had changed?

interesting_anyway.title: What would you probably still find interesting even if nobody could tell you yet whether a good business comes out of it?
interesting_anyway.hint: It does not have to be an idea. A topic is enough.

followUps.whatYouWouldFindOutFirst: What would you want to find out about it first?

five_years_back.title: Looking back from five years out: what would have to exist or be different because of your work for you to think: that was worth the effort?
five_years_back.hint: A direction, not a job title.

followUps.whatDependsOnYou: Which part of that depends on you — and which does not?
followUps.whatYouWouldGiveUp: What would you accept in return for it?

statements.title: My direction
statements.text: What you keep here belongs to you — in your words. It is visible only to you, and no number comes out of it.
statements.empty: Nothing kept yet. Write down what struck you while reading your answers.
statements.statementPlaceholder: For example: making complicated systems easier to understand
statements.statementHint: At most {max} characters. A direction you cannot say in one sentence is not one yet.

facets.meaningful_outcome: Outcomes that mean something to me
facets.preferred_contribution: How I most like to contribute

statements.pendingProposals: There are no proposals from your answers yet — until then you write down yourself what you notice.
